preamble: In central and northwestern Iranian Persian, especially around Tehran, the inherited uvular stop /q/ (qāf, mostly in Arabic and Turkic loans) has merged with /ɣ/ (ghayn). The merged phoneme is usually a voiced uvular stop [ɢ], but between vowels in unstressed position it is realized as a fricative, described as velar [ɣ] or uvular [ʁ]. Outside Persian, fricative realizations of qāf (Sudanese, some Yemeni Arabic) are uvular [ʁ] and belong under q > ʁ.

examples.note: After the merger of /q/ with /ɣ/ the phoneme is a fricative between vowels; Wiktionary transcribes this word with uvular [ʁ], and Wikipedia gives the intervocalic fricative as velar [ɣ] or uvular [ʁ]. Dari and Tajik keep [q].
